title: Slice flakiness hedging and traffic priming notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick, messy brain-dump for a lightweight complement to our existing rollout playbooks: a small set of tactics to reduce noisy signal (slice flakiness) and to ‘prime’ traffic so canaries / A/B cohorts converge faster with fewer false alarms. This is specifically aimed at latency/cost-sensitive LLM routes where behavioral variability + low sample sizes create churn for stewards.

Key ideas (sketch):
- Traffic priming: send carefully-crafted warm requests to a new slice before enabling live user traffic. Warm = short, high-signal prompts that exercise core code paths (cache keys, kv-population). Purpose: reduce cold-start variability and get initial telemetry baseline.
- Flakiness hedging: detect slices with high within-slice variance on short windows and automatically reduce weight + run synthetic probes rather than full rollback. Hedge > immediate revert.
- Micro-epochs: split early exposure into X micro-epochs (e.g., 10x 0.1% increments) with explicit short wait windows for signal smoothing. Avoid long waits per epoch but prefer repeated tiny exposures to smooth variance.
- Synthetic probes + golden prompts: maintain a small set of deterministic prompts per product surface (rerank, chat, completion) used to surface behavioral drift independent of user noise.

Operational checklist (minimal runbook):
1) Preflight: pick target slice(s), identify golden prompts, ensure canary model variant + quantization flagged. Open rollout ticket (JIRA).
2) Priming: send 50-200 golden probes scoped to the slice; verify KV cache warm and latency stable. Record pre-priming baseline.
3) Micro-epochs: enable 0.1% traffic for 5m, run signal aggregation (latency p50/p95, error rate, quality regressions from eval harness), then increase if stable. Repeat up to safety threshold.
4) Hedge logic: if variance in quality metric > threshold OR p95 latency oscillates > X ms across 3 micro-epochs, automatically trigger hedging: reduce weight to previous stable point, run extra synthetic probes, notify steward.
5) Escalation: if hedging fails or quality delta > absolute threshold, follow full rollback and incident playbook.

Signal set (prioritized):
- Primary: model quality delta on golden prompts (token-level log-prob delta, ranking precision), synthetic-output regression rate.
- Secondary: latency p50/p95, tail CPU/GPU utilization, error codes (429/503) from serving runtime.
- Tertiary: product-level metrics (CTR for reranker, completion accept rate) but treat as noisy during first micro-epochs.

Decision heuristics (draft numbers, needs tuning):
- Accept if quality delta on golden prompts < 0.5% and latency p95 delta < 50ms across 3 consecutive micro-epochs.
- Hedge if quality delta between 0.5% and 2% OR variance > 1.2x historical slice variance.
- Rollback if quality delta > 2.0% OR any catastrophic error spike (error rate > 1%) OR sustained p95 delta > 200ms.

Instrumentation and tooling needs:
- Console: micro-epoch timer & quick ‘prime now’ button (UI) + synthetic-probe log viewer.
- Telemetry: sample-by-slice variance metric, golden-prompt regression pipeline, and short-run A/B bootstrap CI.
- Automations: hedging policy as a first-class policy in routing layer (reduce weight, route to synthetic probe runner, re-evaluate).

Roles & responsibilities:
- Steward: product or eng PM who owns the slice activation and is on-call during exposure window.
- Observer: SRE/observability to validate infra signals and confirm if hedging is infra-related.
- Fallback owner: serving-runtime lead to troubleshoot model runtime regressions.

Open questions / unknowns (todo):
- How many golden probes are enough to be stable across model sizes and prompts? (Priya to run small sweep)
- Best thresholds for variance hedging per-route; can we auto-calibrate using historical slice-level noise? (Diego exploring)
- Cost tradeoffs: how expensive will priming be for high-throughput endpoints? Need quick cost estimator in Optimize.
- Interaction with dedicated/private customers: do we allow automated hedging for Dedicated pools or require manual steward approval?

Small experiments to run (next 2 sprints):
- A: Implement synthetic-probe runner and run priming on 3 small slices (search-rerank, short-chat, summarization) and compare cold vs primed micro-epoch variance.
- B: Collect per-slice within-epoch variance and test auto-calibration algorithm (k-means on variance buckets).
- C: UX test: add ‘prime now’ control in Console and run with 2 pilot customers.

Notes to self / reminders:
- Keep this doc lightweight; aim for a single-page Canvas for runbook once we validate.
- Don’t over-index on product metrics early — they’re noisy. Use synthetic prompts + short CI.
- Link to existing canary playbooks and SLOs when migrating to full rollout flow.

References and quick links:
- Confluence: ROLL-4352 (flakiness hedging design)
- JIRA: OPS-1287 (synthetic-probe runner)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/256 (console priming button prototype)

If you're reading this and want to prototype, ping me in #console-rollouts or drop a note on the JIRA card. This is deliberately fuzzy — objective is to bake a low-friction, low-cost hedge so stewards see fewer false rollbacks.
